posts.title: When decadal dry-wet swings cluster
posts.text: Five lake records from China, decomposed with EMD and the Hilbert transform: decadal dry-wet shifts over the last millennium were more frequent where the centennial-scale contrast was larger.
posts.alt: Schematic chart on a light background: five lake names in rows, with filled dots showing whether decadal dry-wet shifts were more frequent in the Medieval Climate Anomaly column or the Little Ice Age column.

posts.title: A lake that drained around 9 ka
posts.text: A 58 m ICDP core from the Lago Maggiore system: ice retreat, glaciolacustrine silts, then sudden delta progradation attributed to a dam breach and lake-level drop at about 9 ka. The site fell dry around 7 ka.
posts.alt: Schematic sediment core column on a light background with four layers: a coarse base, about 35 m of silts and sands, sandier lake deposits above a dashed line marked ca. 9 ka (dam breach, lake-level drop), and colluvium at the top.
